extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers, policymakers and diplomats interested in postwar atomic control and international affairs
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting and summarization of competing national proposals (Soviet, British, U.S. majority plan) and recommended provisions for an international system and agency to control atomic energy and prohibit atomic weapons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong and comprehensive international system for control and prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a strong and comprehensive international system for the control of atomic energy and the prohibition of atomic weapons, aimed at attaining the objectives set forth in the General Assembly resolution of 24 January, 1946.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an international system should be established; its scope and the treaty should embrace the entire program for putting the international system of control into effect and should provide for simultaneous establishment of strict international control over all facilities engaged in mining atomic raw materials and production of atomic materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of an International Control Agency/Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be established an International Control Agency (International Control Commission) with powers of inspection and control over atomic energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission shall have its own machinery for inspection, its own rules of procedure, and may be given necessary powers to carry out its functions; drafts of a convention and agency should be concluded and brought into effect simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency research and development responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) The agency should have positive research and development responsibilities in order to remain in the forefront of atomic energy knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These responsibilities ensure the agency can render itself more effective in promoting beneficial peaceful uses of atomic energy and in eliminating destructive uses; the agency must keep itself informed on latest achievements and have skilled international personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and exchange of basic scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should promote among all nations the exchange of basic scientific information on atomic energy for peaceful ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guided by the general principle that there should be no secrecy among nations as to basic scientific information; the Commission should ensure a wide exchange of information and render assistance through advice to countries that request it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency power to investigate clandestine activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should have the duty of seeking out any clandestine activities or facilities involving source material or nuclear fuel and the power to require reports and obtain information it deems necessary by direct means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To this end it should have power to requisition reports, verify them, obtain further information, and carry out special investigations in cases of suspected violations; investigations must be effective to prevent diversion of dangerous materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency access to facilities and unimpeded rights for representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Accredited representatives of the agency should be afforded unimpeded rights of ingress, egress, and access to facilities for mining, production, stockpiling, and exploitation located within participating nations' territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access applies to facilities for mining atomic raw materials and the production and stockpiling of atomic materials; representatives should be unhindered by national or local authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection powers and technical measures
rubrics_metrics.description: For fulfillment of control and inspection tasks, the International Control Commission shall have the right to carry out weighing, measurements and various analyses of atomic raw materials, atomic materials and unfinished products, and to study production operations as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection duties include checking existing stocks, studying production operations, observing technical exploitation rules, checking accounts, and performing necessary measurements and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority to request data and explanations from governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall have the right to request from any government various data and reports on the activities of atomic energy facilities and to request explanations on questions relating to those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes requiring reports on relevant matters and other information as it deems necessary to discharge inspection and control functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency recommendations to governments and Security Council
rubrics_metrics.description: (g) Make recommendations to governments on questions relating to the production, stockpiling, and use of atomic materials and atomic energy; (h) Make recommendations to the Security Council on measures for prevention and suppression with regard to violators of the conventions on prohibition and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency should submit recommendations and suggestions to governments and the Security Council concerning violators and appropriate measures to prevent and suppress violations and evasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency custody or trust over source materials and dangerous facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The agency should hold all the atomic source materials, nuclear fuels and dangerous facilities in trust for the participating nations, responsible for insuring that treaty provisions are observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding materials in trust is presented as a means to ensure effective protection against sudden diversion or use; the plan envisions agency control/management of dangerous facilities to prevent unauthorized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and operation of facilities under agency authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and technical research, and potentially some facilities, may be operated by nations or persons under license from the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency's functions may include licensing operators of facilities and ensuring exploratory/peaceful operations conform to treaty obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and elimination of atomic weapons
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) International agreement to outlaw the national production and use of atomic weapons is an essential part of the international system of control; (b) manufacture, possession and use of atomic weapons by all nations and persons should be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All existing stocks of finished and unfinished atomic weapons should be destroyed promptly (text mentions within three months of date of entry into force) and measures taken to prevent diversion; prohibition applies universally to states and persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional step-by-step treaty implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The treaty should provide an orderly and agreed sequence of steps (a transitional step-by-step program) for putting the international system of control into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A phased approach is advocated so that conventions and control measures can be concluded and implemented simultaneously and effectively, with the Commission having authority to take necessary steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel selection and international composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The personnel of the agency/International Control Commission shall be recruited and selected on an international basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection on an international basis is meant to ensure impartiality, provide skilled international personnel, and support the Commission's practical execution of control and inspection measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific research constraints and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Scientific research activities in atomic energy must comply with the necessity of carrying out the convention on prohibition of atomic weapons and preventing military purposes; (b) Signatory states must have the right to carry out unrestricted scientific research directed toward discovery of methods for peaceful uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research by states is allowed for peaceful objectives but must be consistent with the convention; the Commission itself should be enabled to carry out research to keep informed and maintain skilled personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency material facilities for research and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Control Commission must have at its disposal material facilities, including research laboratories and experimental installations, necessary for the proper organization of research activities to be conducted by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession of research facilities enables the Commission to conduct investigations, keep abreast of technical developments, and provide technical assistance to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special investigations on suspicion of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) Carry out special investigations in cases when suspicion of violations of the convention on the prohibition of atomic weapons and on the control of atomic energy arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission should have authority and procedures to launch and carry out targeted inquiries when clandestine activity or suspected violations are reported or detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Majority Plan enforcement features (no veto; severe punishment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Majority Plan provides for an international atomic commission with control over the atom from mine to finished product, severe punishment of nations breaking atomic control, and it does not have any veto on its decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts with proposals that would allow veto power for great powers; enforcement via punitive measures and an absence of veto are presented as means to ensure effective multilateral control.
